# arcane_api_subresource (Data Source)

Reads a subresource of an Arcane object with `GET <object>/<subresource>`.

The request is sent on every plan, apply and refresh, and the result is kept in state. For secrets such as short-lived tokens, use the `arcane_api_subresource` ephemeral resource, which keeps the result out of the plan and state. The token needs `get` on `<plural>/<subresource>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The request runs on every plan, apply and refresh, and the result is kept in state.
# Use the arcane_api_subresource ephemeral resource for secrets such as tokens.
data "arcane_api_subresource" "permissions" {
  api_version = "flare.pubg.io/v1"
  kind        = "Secret"
  namespace   = "game"
  name        = "db-password"
  subresource = "permissions"
}

output "permissions" {
  value = nonsensitive(data.arcane_api_subresource.permissions.object.spec)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `api_version` (String) apiVersion of the parent resource kind, not of the subresource object, such as `sample.arcane.pubg.io/v1`.
- `kind` (String) Kind of the parent resource, not of the subresource object.
- `name` (String) Name of the parent object.
- `subresource` (String) Name of the subresource, as API discovery lists it for the kind, such as `claim` for `runneridtokens/claim`.

### Optional

- `namespace` (String) Namespace of the parent object. Required for a namespaced kind, and not allowed for a cluster-scoped one.
- `query` (Map of String) Query parameters to send with the GET request. The API server passes them to the subresource as they are.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) API path of the subresource
- `object` (Dynamic, Sensitive) Object the server returned, as an object value, as received. Always sensitive.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
